denomProfiles/syro-malankara-catholic/ta: West Syriac St Thomas Christians who entered Catholic communion with Mar Ivanios in 1930.
denomProfiles/syro-malankara-catholic/co: Catholic faith in full: the seven sacraments, the ecumenical councils and the primacy and infallibility of the Pope (Vatican I, 1870).
Antiochene (West Syriac) liturgical and theological tradition shared with the Malankara Orthodox.
Reunion of Malankara Christians with Rome without abandoning their rite.
denomProfiles/syro-malankara-catholic/fo: Monastic and ashram spirituality, from the Bethany congregations founded by Mar Ivanios.
Evangelisation and social service in south Kerala and Kanyakumari.
Education, including Mar Ivanios College in Thiruvananthapuram.
Ecumenical relations with the Malankara Orthodox and Jacobite churches.
denomProfiles/syro-malankara-catholic/pr: Holy Qurbana of St James in Malayalam, with Syriac chants.
Seven canonical hours of West Syriac prayer (Shehimo).
Bishops titled with 'Mar' and the West Syriac vestments of the Malankara tradition.
denomProfiles/syro-malankara-catholic/in: Its ashram model contributed to inculturation debates in Indian Christianity.
Shared liturgy keeps close ties with other Malankara churches.
denomProfiles/syro-malankara-catholic/ke: Founder of the Bethany movement (1919) and leader of the 1930 reunion
Bishop who joined the reunion with Mar Ivanios
Major Archbishop since 2007 and cardinal since 2012

denomProfiles/syro-malankara-catholic/in: Based in Kerala, headquartered at Pattom, Thiruvananthapuram, with the Eparchy of Marthandam (1996) serving Kanyakumari district in Tamil Nadu and jurisdictions across India and abroad.
denomProfiles/coptic-catholic/tagline: Egypt's Catholic church of the Alexandrian rite, strong in schools and Upper Egypt.
denomProfiles/coptic-catholic/coreDoctri: Catholic faith in full: the seven sacraments, the ecumenical councils and the primacy and infallibility of the Pope (Vatican I, 1870).
Alexandrian (Coptic) theological heritage of Athanasius and Cyril, held with Chalcedonian Christology.
A patriarchate of Alexandria in communion with Rome, restored in 1895.
Shared faith in Christ with the Coptic Orthodox, recognised in the Paul VI–Shenouda III declaration (1973).
denomProfiles/coptic-catholic/focuses/0: Education and healthcare, especially in Upper Egypt.
denomProfiles/coptic-catholic/focuses/1: Christian presence in a Muslim-majority society.
denomProfiles/coptic-catholic/focuses/2: Relations with the far larger Coptic Orthodox Church.
denomProfiles/coptic-catholic/focuses/3: Pastoral work among the poor through religious congregations.
denomProfiles/coptic-catholic/practices/: Coptic liturgies of St Basil, St Gregory and St Cyril in Coptic and Arabic.
Coptic chant with cymbals and triangle.
Long Coptic fasts, though often lightened compared with Orthodox practice.
denomProfiles/coptic-catholic/influenced: Catholic schools in Egypt educated many Christian and Muslim leaders.
The church is a local partner in Catholic–Coptic relations.
denomProfiles/coptic-catholic/keyFigures: Coptic bishop of Jerusalem who joined Rome in 1741
First patriarch of the restored patriarchate (1899)
denomProfiles/coptic-catholic/members/no: CNEWA, The Eastern Catholic Churches 2017 (statistical table compiled from the Annuario Pontificio).
denomProfiles/ethiopian-eritrean-catholi: Catholic churches of the Ge'ez (Alexandrian) rite in Ethiopia and Eritrea.
Catholic faith in full: the seven sacraments, the ecumenical councils and the primacy and infallibility of the Pope (Vatican I, 1870).
Ethiopian Ge'ez liturgical and spiritual heritage, shared with the Orthodox Tewahedo churches.
Two self-governing metropolitan churches: Addis Ababa (from 1961) and Asmara (separate since 2015).
Chalcedonian Christology held within a non-Chalcedonian liturgical inheritance.
Schools, clinics and development work far beyond their small numbers.
Humanitarian care during famine, war and displacement.
Recovering authentic Ge'ez practice after earlier Latinisation.
Relations with the dominant Orthodox Tewahedo churches.
Qeddase (Eucharistic liturgy) in Ge'ez, Amharic, Tigrinya and other languages.
Ethiopian chant (zema) and the liturgical drum and sistrum.
Ethiopian fasts and calendar.
Married priests alongside celibate religious.
Eritrean Catholic Church
Raised to its own metropolitan church sui iuris in 2015.
Ethiopian education
Catholic schools and colleges contributed to modern education in both countries.

denomProfiles/armenian-catholic/tagline: Armenian-rite Catholic church of the Patriarchate of Cilicia, seated in Lebanon.
denomProfiles/armenian-catholic/coreDoct: Catholic faith in full: the seven sacraments, the ecumenical councils and the primacy and infallibility of the Pope (Vatican I, 1870).
Armenian theological heritage of Gregory the Illuminator, Mesrop Mashtots and Gregory of Narek.
Patriarchate of Cilicia in communion with Rome since 1742.
Gregory of Narek declared a Doctor of the Church by Pope Francis (2015).
denomProfiles/armenian-catholic/focuses/: Preserving Armenian language, culture and memory, including of the 1915 genocide.
Scholarship, through the Mekhitarist monks of Venice and Vienna.
Communities in Lebanon, Syria, Armenia, Europe and the Americas.
Relations with the Armenian Apostolic Church.
denomProfiles/armenian-catholic/practice: Armenian Divine Liturgy (Badarak) in Classical Armenian.
Unleavened bread and wine without water, as in Armenian tradition.
Mostly celibate clergy, with some married priests.
denomProfiles/armenian-catholic/influenc: Founded by Mekhitar of Sebaste (1701), it shaped modern Armenian scholarship and printing.
Both churches are based in Lebanon and share Cilician heritage.
denomProfiles/armenian-catholic/keyFigur: First Patriarch of Cilicia in union with Rome (1742)
Founder of the Mekhitarist monks at San Lazzaro, Venice
Archbishop of Mardin killed in 1915, canonised in 2025
denomProfiles/armenian-catholic/members/: CNEWA, The Eastern Catholic Churches 2017 (statistical table compiled from the Annuario Pontificio).
denomProfiles/syriac-catholic/tagline: West Syriac Catholic church of Antioch, rooted in Iraq, Syria and Lebanon.
denomProfiles/syriac-catholic/coreDoctri: Catholic faith in full: the seven sacraments, the ecumenical councils and the primacy and infallibility of the Pope (Vatican I, 1870).
Antiochene Syriac heritage of Ephrem and Jacob of Serugh, shared with the Syriac Orthodox Church.
Patriarchate of Antioch in communion with Rome, continuous since 1782.
Chalcedonian Christology within a Syriac liturgical tradition.
denomProfiles/syriac-catholic/focuses/0: Survival of communities in Iraq's Nineveh Plains, especially Qaraqosh (Bakhdida), after the 2014 Islamic State expulsions.
denomProfiles/syriac-catholic/focuses/1: Rebuilding churches and homes after war in Iraq and Syria.
denomProfiles/syriac-catholic/focuses/2: Preserving the Syriac language and chant.
denomProfiles/syriac-catholic/focuses/3: Diaspora communities in Europe, North America and Australia.
denomProfiles/syriac-catholic/practices/: Divine Liturgy of St James in Syriac and Arabic.
Married priests in the Middle East.
Patriarch resident in Beirut, with the patriarchal monastery at Charfet.
denomProfiles/syriac-catholic/influenced: It shares the West Syriac rite of the Syriac Catholic Church.
Clergy such as Patriarch Ignatius Ephrem II Rahmani edited Syriac texts.
denomProfiles/syriac-catholic/keyFigures: Patriarch from 1782, founder of Charfet monastery
denomProfiles/ruthenian-catholic/tagline: Byzantine Catholics of the Carpathians and their American Metropolia of Pittsburgh.
denomProfiles/ruthenian-catholic/coreDoc: Catholic faith in full: the seven sacraments, the ecumenical councils and the primacy and infallibility of the Pope (Vatican I, 1870).
Byzantine Slavic heritage of Cyril and Methodius in the Carpathian region.
Union with Rome through the Union of Uzhhorod (1646).
Self-governing metropolitan church in the United States since 1969.
denomProfiles/ruthenian-catholic/focuses: Carpatho-Rusyn identity in Transcarpathian Ukraine, Slovakia and the United States.
Recovery from Soviet suppression of the Mukachevo eparchy (1949–89).
Restoring Eastern practice after earlier Latinisation in America.
English-language Byzantine liturgy for American parishes.
denomProfiles/ruthenian-catholic/practic: Divine Liturgy of St John Chrysostom in Church Slavonic and English.
Married priests, again permitted in North America since 2014.
Pascha baskets blessed at Easter and other Carpathian customs.
denomProfiles/ruthenian-catholic/influen: Alexis Toth led thousands of Ruthenian immigrants into Orthodoxy after 1891.
Formed in 1938 by Ruthenians who rejected the ban on married priests (1929).
denomProfiles/ruthenian-catholic/keyFigu: Bishop of Mukachevo killed in 1947, beatified 2001
Priest who led a movement into Orthodoxy, later canonised by the Orthodox
First Ruthenian bishop in the United States (1924)
denomProfiles/ruthenian-catholic/members: CNEWA, The Eastern Catholic Churches 2017 (statistical table compiled from the Annuario Pontificio).
denomProfiles/polish-national-catholic/t: Polish-American Catholic church founded at Scranton in 1897, independent of Rome.
denomProfiles/polish-national-catholic/c: Catholic faith of the undivided church, independent of papal jurisdiction.
The Word of God heard and preached counted as a sacrament, alongside baptism and confirmation.
Real presence of Christ in the Eucharist.
Rejects papal infallibility; teaches that God's grace may reach the unbaptised after death.
Parish property owned and governed by the parishioners.
denomProfiles/polish-national-catholic/f: Polish ethnic identity and lay control of parishes.
Democratic synods of clergy and laity.
Conservative stance on women's ordination and sexuality, which led it to leave the Union of Utrecht in 2003.
Dialogue with the Roman Catholic Church.
denomProfiles/polish-national-catholic/p: General confession for adults, with private confession for the young.
Feasts of its own, such as the Brotherhood of Man.
denomProfiles/polish-national-catholic/i: A daughter church founded by PNCC missionaries after 1920.
An association it founded in 2008 with churches that left Utrecht.
denomProfiles/independent-catholic/tagli: Small Catholic-style churches led by bishops outside Rome and Utrecht.
denomProfiles/independent-catholic/coreD: Claim to valid apostolic succession, mostly through Old Catholic, Syrian or Roman Catholic bishops.
Catholic sacraments and creeds, interpreted in widely varying ways.
Positions range from traditionalist and sedevacantist to progressive and theosophical (Liberal Catholic Church).
denomProfiles/independent-catholic/focus: Sacramental ministry to people outside or alienated from the Catholic Church.
Inclusion of divorced, remarried and LGBT Catholics in many progressive bodies.
Ethnic and national churches, such as the Brazilian Catholic Apostolic Church (1945).
Small house churches and part-time clergy.
denomProfiles/independent-catholic/pract: Mass in Roman, Tridentine or revised forms.
Married clergy; women ordained in many progressive groups.
Ordinations and consecrations often conferred freely, producing many 'bishops at large'.
Highly fragmented jurisdictions, often of a few congregations.
denomProfiles/independent-catholic/influ: Founded in 1916 by James Wedgwood and Charles Leadbeater with theosophical teaching.
Consecrations by Archbishop Ngô Đình Thục (1981) seeded several traditionalist lines.
denomProfiles/independent-catholic/keyFi: Founder of many American independent lines
Zambian archbishop who consecrated married bishops in 2006
denomProfiles/independent-catholic/inInd: The movement has a South Asian root: Antonio Alvares, a Goan priest consecrated by Syrian Orthodox bishops in 1889 as head of an independent church in Goa and Ceylon, consecrated Vilatte in 1892.
